Using the correct identity,
\[
\sin^2 A+\sin^2 C=1+2\cos^2 B.
\]
Together with \(\cos^2 A+\cos^2 C=1-2\cos^2 B\), this gives
\[
\cos B\bigl(\cos(A-C)-2\cos B\bigr)=0.
\]
If \(\cos B\ne 0\), then \(\cos(A-C)=2\cos B\), so
\[
\cos A\cos C=\frac12\cos B,\qquad \sin A\sin C=\frac32\cos B,
\]
hence \(\tan A\tan C=3\).

If \(\cos B=0\), then \(B=90^\circ\), so \(A+C=90^\circ\) and \(\tan A\tan C=1\).

Thus the condition does not determine a unique value:
\[
\boxed{\text{not uniquely determined: }1\text{ or }3}
\]
(If the intended assumption is \(\cos B\ne 0\), the answer is \(\boxed{3}\).)
